DEF-006 — ENTRANCE DOOR ON THE NORTH FACE
The overnight build put the main door on the street-facing NORTH wall,
≈8 blocks off the x=0 drive axis. The plan called for the principal
entrance on the SOUTH (+Z), addressing the drive. Logged cosmetic;
the door face has not yet been RCON-confirmed.

THE GUEST & DESIGN CENTER
Two storeys · 44,019 SF (verified) · the anchor at the head of the showcase street · isometric massing mockup
Drawn to the RCON-measured as-built shell — 141 × ≥90 blocks, y63 → y79, hollow — with the entrance drive running south to z ≈ +200
AS-BUILT SOURCE
qa/as-built-survey.md — live-server RCON, 2026-07-24
open defects: DEF-002 footprint · DEF-005 road block · DEF-006 door face
MEASURED SECTION — WHAT THE PROBES ACTUALLY FOUND
gray_concrete roof band (y76–79)
upper storey — walls present, interior NOT probed
lower storey — interior AIR confirmed y65–68
polished_andesite floor · sea_lantern lighting
stone_brick foundation (y62–63)
band depths are drawn for legibility, not to scale · solid outline = directly probed, dashed = never probed
STILL UNRESOLVED IN THE SURVEY
The Guest Center wall block was never identified — walls are drawn a neutral stone grey.
Depth is a lower bound: the probe reported “z ~90…180+”, so the south face is not pinned.
The 141-wide plate is far larger than either planned scheme (75×75 / 90×60) — DEF-002 open.
The y=63 surface at x=0 between z 90–180 may be Guest Center floor rather than road.
Windows, doors, glazing bays, the forecourt apron and all landscaping are invented here.
Nothing at all is built of the monument, parking field, cooking school or warehouse.
MASSING MOCKUP — NOT A SCREENSHOT
Hand-drawn isometric massing study of a block shell. Not a render, not a capture of the running world.
VERIFIED: 44,019 SF / 2 storeys / “Class A mansion” massing; and the as-built shell dimensions, the hollow section and the four materials named above — all probed block-by-block on 2026-07-24.
CREATIVE APPROXIMATION: the wall material, every window and door opening, the forecourt apron, the landscaping, the monument, and the “Tuscan stucco welcome centre” styling in planning/palettes.yaml.
No retrieved source documents what this building actually looked like (REF-019).
